title: Body, health and things
theme: the body, medical care, objects and leisure
goal: Recognise and use 21 frequent words for the body and health, everyday objects and leisure.

example.fr: Trop d'alcool, c'est mauvais pour le foie.
example.en: Too much alcohol is bad for the liver.

example.fr: L'infirmière prend mon pouls.
example.en: The nurse is taking my pulse.

example.fr: Arrête de te ronger les ongles !
example.en: Stop biting your nails!

example.fr: Après la chirurgie, il doit se reposer deux semaines.
example.en: After the surgery, he has to rest for two weeks.

items.note: For one specific operation, France usually says une opération; une chirurgie in this sense is common in Québec.

example.fr: La chirurgienne m'a tout expliqué avant l'opération.
example.en: The surgeon explained everything to me before the operation.

example.fr: Ne marche pas pieds nus, le plancher est froid.
example.en: Don't walk barefoot, the floor is cold.

example.fr: Il était ivre au volant ; la police l'a arrêté.
example.en: He was drunk at the wheel; the police stopped him.

example.fr: Il lui a offert une bague de fiançailles.
example.en: He gave her an engagement ring.

example.fr: Elle ne porte plus son alliance.
example.en: She doesn't wear her wedding ring anymore.

items.note: Also: an alliance between groups or countries.

example.fr: Quel parfum de crème glacée tu veux ?
example.en: Which ice-cream flavour do you want?

example.fr: On a ouvert une bouteille de champagne pour fêter ça.
example.en: We opened a bottle of champagne to celebrate.

example.fr: Le matin, je prends un bol de céréales.
example.en: In the morning, I have a bowl of cereal.

items.note: Informal (France): avoir du bol = to be lucky.

example.fr: J'ai acheté une nouvelle paire de bottes d'hiver.
example.en: I bought a new pair of winter boots.

example.fr: Tu veux un morceau de gâteau ?
example.en: Do you want a piece of cake?

items.note: Plural: des morceaux. Also a piece of music, a track.

example.fr: Les enfants se lancent des boules de neige.
example.en: The kids are throwing snowballs at each other.

example.fr: Les cloches de l'église sonnent à midi.
example.en: The church bells ring at noon.

example.fr: Je n'ai pas le câble pour charger mon téléphone.
example.en: I don't have the cable to charge my phone.

example.fr: Mon père a gardé tous ses vieux disques.
example.en: My father kept all his old records.

items.en: screenplay, script; possible course of events

example.fr: Le scénario de ce film est excellent.
example.en: The screenplay of this movie is excellent.

example.fr: Le Cirque du Soleil a été créé au Québec.
example.en: Cirque du Soleil was founded in Québec.

items.en: sport played with clubs on 18 holes

example.fr: Mon beau-père joue au golf tous les dimanches.
example.en: My father-in-law plays golf every Sunday.

blocks.title: Usage tips
blocks.body:
[[Le parfum]] also means *flavour*: [[Quel parfum ?]] at the ice-cream counter.

[[Ivre]] is the neutral word for drunk; [[bourré]] is informal. In [[le pouls]], the l and s are silent: [pu]. [[Pieds nus]] = barefoot. A wedding ring is [[une alliance]]; any other ring is [[une bague]].

lines.en: The nurse is taking my pulse.

lines.fr: Arrête de te ronger les ongles !
Après la chirurgie, il doit se reposer deux semaines.
lines.en: After the surgery, he has to rest for two weeks.
lines.tip: ch in chirurgie sounds like sh.

lines.fr: Ne marche pas pieds nus, le plancher est froid.
lines.en: Don't walk barefoot, the floor is cold.

lines.en: He gave her an engagement ring.

lines.fr: Quel parfum de crème glacée tu veux ?
lines.en: Which ice-cream flavour do you want?

lines.fr: Tu veux un morceau de gâteau ?
lines.en: Do you want a piece of cake?

lines.fr: Les cloches de l'église sonnent à midi.
lines.en: The church bells ring at noon.

lines.en: I don't have the cable to charge my phone.

blocks.prompt: At the ice-cream shop, the server asks: “Quel parfum ?” She wants to know…
blocks.explain: With food, [[le parfum]] means the flavour.

blocks.prompt: Which word is the neutral (not slang) way to say “drunk”?
Do you want a piece of cake? (to a friend)
accept: Tu veux un morceau de gâteau ?
Est-ce que tu veux un morceau de gâteau ?
blocks.explain: [[Un morceau de]] + noun, with no article after de.

blocks.prompt: I bought a pair of boots.
accept: J'ai acheté une paire de bottes.
Je me suis acheté une paire de bottes.

blocks.en: The nurse is taking my pulse.
blocks.explain: [[Prendre le pouls]] = to take someone's pulse.

blocks.en: She doesn't wear her wedding ring anymore.
blocks.explain: [[Alliance]] is feminine, but before a vowel you say [[son alliance]], not *sa*.

blocks.fr: Mon beau-père joue au golf tous les dimanches.
Je n'ai pas le câble pour charger mon téléphone.
blocks.en: I don't have the cable to charge my phone.
options: They don't have a charging cable.
blocks.explain: [[Le câble pour charger]] = the charging cable.

summary:
- Talk about the body and health: [[le foie, le pouls, les ongles, la chirurgie]]
- Name everyday objects: [[une bague, une alliance, un bol, une paire, un morceau]]
- Know that [[le parfum]] can mean *flavour*

meta.author: ai
meta.notes: Rewrote the glosses for champagne, câble, scénario and golf so they no longer repeat the French word; made the chirurgie note more precise (une opération in France, une chirurgie common in Québec); added a valid variant to r6. Cirque du Soleil fact checked (founded in Québec).
